description.short: Capital city; site of government, protest, and national symbols.
description.long: Ufa (Өфө) is the capital of Bashkortostan, where the constitution lives and breathes. Here the Eagle of First Intellect watches over civic identity, legal sovereignty, and the ongoing struggle for language rights. The parliament building stands as a monument to the people's power.
description.ibn_arabi_connection: The Eagle represents the First Intellect (al-'Aql al-Awwal) — the primordial light of knowledge from which all understanding flows. At Ufa, we encounter the constitutional knowledge that defines a people.

stations.name: The Parliament Steps
stations.display_name: Parliament Steps – Where Laws Take Flight
stations.opening_meditation: You stand before the parliament of Bashkortostan. The Eagle descends from the sky, carrying the constitution in its talons. 'Voyager,' it speaks, 'here begins your journey into the heart of a nation. Every word you learn is a feather in your wings. Every phrase, a step toward understanding.' The doors open. What will you discover?
stations.closing_meditation: You have walked the Parliament Steps. Six words now live within you — Bashkortostan, people, freedom, language, constitution, and the hero Ural-Batyr. The Eagle nods. 'Remember: the journey made within yourself leads to yourself.' Rest now. The Fountain awaits.

description.short: Paleolithic sanctuary with ancient paintings; gateway to Bashkir mythos.
description.long: Shulgan-Tash (Kapova Cave) holds 14,000-year-old paintings — the oldest art in Eastern Europe. Here the Crow of Universal Body guards ancestral memory. The underground river Shulgan flows through darkness into light. This is where time collapses and the ancestors speak.
description.ibn_arabi_connection: The Crow represents Universal Body (al-Jism al-Kulli) — matter infused with spirit, darkness containing lights. In the cave's depths, we find manifestation: the physical traces of spiritual vision painted on stone.

stations.name: The Cave Mouth
stations.opening_meditation: You enter Shulgan-Tash. The Crow awaits on a stalactite, its black feathers absorbing even the torchlight. 'Voyager,' it croaks, 'I am the keeper of what was. Every word I guard is a fossil of meaning, preserved for 14,000 years.' The paintings begin to glow. What stories will you hear?
stations.closing_meditation: You emerge from the Cave Mouth. Six words now echo in your bones — sun, moon, stone, water, river, and the sacred Agidel. The Crow folds its wings. 'What you have learned is not new. It was always within you, waiting to be remembered.' The mountain calls.

description.short: Sacred mountain; symbol of endurance and hidden strength.
description.long: Yamantau ('Bad Mountain') rises 1,640 meters — the highest peak in the Southern Urals. Its name warns of danger, but the Anqa knows: transformation requires fire. Here, in the realm of Prime Matter, potential awaits activation. The mountain tests those who approach.
description.ibn_arabi_connection: The Anqa represents Prime Matter (al-Hayūlā) — pure potentiality, the 'name without a body.' Like the mythical phoenix, it exists in the realm of possibility. At Yamantau, we encounter words of power, danger, and transformation.

stations.name: The Summit Path
stations.opening_meditation: You climb toward Yamantau. The Anqa circles above, a creature of flame and mystery. 'Voyager,' its voice echoes, 'I am what might be. Every word you learn here holds danger — and within danger, transformation.' The wind howls. The forest darkens. Do you dare continue?
stations.closing_meditation: You stand at the treeline of Yamantau. Seven words now burn within you — mountain, wind, forest, danger, lake, bad, and big. The Anqa alights beside you. 'The name means Bad Mountain, yet you have gained good things. This is the secret: from danger, wisdom.' The forge awaits.

description.short: Historic metallurgical center; represents Bashkir labor identity.
description.long: Beloretsk has forged steel since 1762. The Ringdove of Universal Soul nests here among the furnaces, finding warmth in industry. This is where raw materials become tools, where labor transforms nature, where the hands of craftsmen shape the future.
description.ibn_arabi_connection: The Ringdove represents Universal Soul (al-Nafs al-Kulliyya) — the receptive, nurturing principle that brings potential into form. At Beloretsk, raw ore becomes steel through the soul's patient work of transformation.

stations.name: The Iron Works
stations.display_name: Iron Works – Where Matter Takes Shape
stations.opening_meditation: You enter Beloretsk's ancient iron works. The Ringdove coos from a beam above the cooling furnace. 'Voyager,' it sings, 'I am the soul that shapes. Every word you learn here was forged in fire and patience.' Sparks fly upward. The hammer falls. What will you create?
stations.closing_meditation: You leave the Iron Works with soot on your hands and steel in your heart. Four words now ring like anvils — work, steel, craftsman, factory. The Ringdove preens its feathers. 'What is made with love endures. What is learned with patience remains.' The village calls.

description.short: Traditional aul preserving language, song, and hospitality.
description.long: Bizhbulyak (Бижбуляк) represents the heart of Bashkir village life — where language lives in daily speech, where honey is shared with guests, where the kuray plays at sunset. The Ringdove makes its true home here, among family and tradition. This is where the soul finds rest.
description.ibn_arabi_connection: The Ringdove at the hearth embodies the Universal Soul in its most nurturing aspect — the warmth of community, the bonds of family, the preservation of tradition through love. Here, language is not learned but lived.

stations.name: The Village Hearth
stations.opening_meditation: You enter Bizhbulyak as the sun sets golden over the fields. The Ringdove waits on the windowsill of a wooden house, smoke rising from the chimney. 'Voyager,' it coos, 'I am the soul of home. Every word you learn here tastes of honey and sounds like family.' The door opens. You are welcomed. What will you share?
stations.closing_meditation: You leave the Village Hearth with honey on your lips and warmth in your heart. Ten words now nestle within you — honey, father, mother, house, kuray, horse, festival, good, small, beautiful. The Ringdove accompanies you to the gate. 'You are no longer a stranger. You carry our words; you are part of our story.' The journey has transformed you.
stations.mnemonic_theme: family, food, music, hospitality, daily life
